summary: Shohei Ohtani represents a truly historic commercial and athletic phenomenon. As a dual-threat superstar who dominates Major League Baseball as both an elite pitcher and hitter, he has achieved a level of sports cultural gravity not seen since Babe Ruth. Currently playing for the Los Angeles Dodgers, Ohtani is a four-time MVP (2021, 2023, 2024, 2025) and back-to-back World Series champion (2024, 2025). His commercial standing is unparalleled in active team sports, with a projected record-breaking $125 million in endorsement income in 2026, partnering with over 20 global brands including New Balance, Hugo Boss, Porsche, and Japan Airlines. Despite a brief period of brand uncertainty during his former interpreter's legal issues in 2024, federal investigations completely cleared Ohtani, reinforcing his market reputation as a highly disciplined, premium brand asset. Though his 2026 pitching campaign was cut short due to a September injured list placement for biceps inflammation, his massive global footprint—specifically spanning North America and East Asia—retains absolute tier-one marketability with steady public attention and immense pricing power.

Ohtani won back-to-back World Series with the Dodgers (2024, 2025) and was unanimously voted the NL MVP in both seasons, raising his career total to four MVPs.

evidence.claim: Ohtani went on the 15-day injured list on September 11, 2026, due to right biceps inflammation, following a 2026 season where he batted .277 with 30 HR and went 8-2 with a 1.79 ERA on the mound.
Ohtani was completely cleared of involvement in the gambling scandal of former interpreter Ippei Mizuhara, who was sentenced to 57 months in prison in February 2025.
